summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of cerebrovascular accident, tracheostomy, GJ tube, and chronic indwelling Foley catheter was admitted from his nursing home for fever and leukocytosis. He was evaluated for sepsis with possible sources including urinary tract infection and aspiration pneumonia. Despite negative urine cultures, he was treated for suspected urosepsis and aspiration pneumonia with IV cefepime and vancomycin, along with oral levofloxacin. A PICC line was placed for continued outpatient antibiotic therapy but required repositioning due to initial malposition. He remained afebrile, with improving respiratory status and resolving leukocytosis. His warfarin was held initially due to supratherapeutic INR and later restarted at an increased dose of 3 mg daily due to subtherapeutic levels. Pressure ulcers were managed with optimized wound care and pain control. He was discharged to extended care with a PICC line to complete a four-day course of antibiotics, instructions for INR monitoring, and ongoing wound and medication management.
